column1: Heat sunflower oil in a deep pan over high heat.
Peel the potatoes, slice into thin rounds and fry about 10 minutes until fully cooked. Drain on a paper-towel-lined tray.
Slice the eggplants and zucchini into thin rounds and fry in the same oil for 5–10 minutes, then drain on the tray.
For the meat sauce, heat the olive oil in a pot over high heat and add the coarsely chopped onion.
Add the minced garlic, thyme, cloves, cinnamon and sugar and cook 2–3 minutes until lightly caramelized.
Add the ground beef, break it up and brown well.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook briefly, then add the tomatoes, lower the heat and simmer 5–10 minutes until thick.
Take off the heat, stir in the chopped parsley and basil, and season with salt and pepper.
For the béchamel, melt the butter in a pot over medium heat, whisk in the flour, then add the milk gradually while whisking until smooth.
Once thick and bubbling, remove from the heat and whisk in the nutmeg, salt, pepper, 100g parmesan and the egg yolks.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C) on fan.
In a 25x32 cm baking dish layer the potatoes, then the eggplant, then the zucchini, seasoning between layers.
Mix 2–3 tablespoons of béchamel into the meat sauce and spread it over the vegetables.
Spread the remaining béchamel on top and sprinkle with the remaining 50g parmesan.
Bake 35–40 minutes until golden, then let cool before serving with fresh herbs and a drizzle of olive oil.
